# Type Alias: AgentActionId

> **AgentActionId** = `string`

Identifies one accepted [`AgentAction`] end to end: returned by the
control endpoint, written as the JSON-RPC request id on the action's wire
frame, and read back off that frame as `request_id` on the folded message
it derives.

A v7 uuid, so ids sort by mint time. Minted by the server at accept time,
or by a client that speculated the action and named it in the control
request - either way the server is the only writer of runtime-bound

not uuids and stay `None`.

# Type Alias: AgentSessionLogEntryDto

> **AgentSessionLogEntryDto** = `LogFrameDto` & \{ `createdAt`: `string`; `id`: `string`; `userId?`: `string` \| `null`; \}

One entry of a session's protocol log.

Serializes as `{"userId": ..., "direction": ..., "content": ...}` - the
frame's own two fields, flattened in beside the attribution, which is the
same shape a recorded session's JSONL carries. A reader can deserialize the
`direction`/`content` pair straight back into the fold's own log type
rather than through a transport vocabulary of its own.

`agentSessionId` is not repeated per entry: every entry in a response
belongs to the session named once at the top.

`Deserialize` is for the wire-contract tests only - nothing server-side
decodes its own response type.

## Type Declaration

| Name | Type | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------ |
| `createdAt` | `string` | When the log recorded the frame. The frame itself carries no time, so this comes from the log row. It is what a reader has to order these against anything else it is showing beside them - the fold derives an order among the messages of one session and nothing more. |
| `id` | `string` | Durable transport row identity; together with `createdAt`, its order cursor. |
| `userId?` | `string` \| `null` | The user whose action produced the frame, absent when no user did. Only prompts carry one, and only when the frame was attributed at the time - a replayed or recorded session's are anonymous. |

Here because a client renders those messages and cannot otherwise work out who sent them: the sender of an agent message is this session's bot, and nothing else names it. | | `entries` | `AgentSessionLogEntryDto`[] | Effective history in ascending `(createdAt, id)` order. The first row is the inclusive history boundary cursor: buffered rows before it are obsolete. Reconcile snapshot overlap by row ID, never content. An empty history has no boundary or overlapping rows. |

There is no sender: a reminder is self-set, so the dispatcher sends it with `sender_id: None` (a recipient who is also the sender is filtered out of their own notification). Every formatter here must therefore work without one. What distinguishes two firings of the same recurring reminder, which are otherwise identical: same id, same description. The collapse key is built from it, so without it Tuesday's alert would replace Monday's unread one on the lock screen. Optional because notifications written before recurring dispatch existed have no such field, and they still have to read back. |

symbols.BotScope:
# Type Alias: BotScope

> **BotScope** = `"user"` \| `"team"`

Access scope for bot-authenticated requests. `user` acts with the
requested-as user's access (requires `requestedAs`); `team` acts with the
bot's owning team's access (team-owned bots only).
symbols.MacroAuth:
# Type Alias: MacroAuth

> **MacroAuth** = \{ `apiKey?`: `never`; `token`: `TokenSource`; `type`: `"user"`; \} \| \{ `apiKey`: `string`; `token?`: `never`; `type`: `"user"`; \} \| \{ `scope?`: `BotScope`; `token`: `TokenSource`; `type`: `"bot"`; \}

How the SDK authenticates with Macro.

A user has exactly one of two credential fields.

- `token`: a bearer token, or a `mak_` API key. The SDK picks the header
  from the prefix at send time.
- `apiKey`: a Settings → API Keys key, always sent as
  `x-macro-user-api-key`. Not prefix-checked, so keys that predate the
  `mak_` prefix work here.

A bot uses an `mbot_` token as `x-macro-bot-token` plus
`x-macro-bot-scope`, defaulting to `user` when `requestedAs` is set and
`team` otherwise.

symbols.QueuedAction:
# Class: QueuedAction

One action waiting in an agent session's server-side queue: a prompt or a
compact accepted while a turn was running, dispatching when that turn
ends. Until then it can be edited (prompts only), steered, or removed; once
it has dispatched, these actions answer 404 — there is no un-sending.

List-sourced only - there is no per-action GET, only the queue snapshot -
so this wraps whatever DTO the caller already has, the same shape
`CrmComment` wraps a list-sourced record, rather than `MacroEntity`'s
lazy-fetch-by-id.

## Accessors

### actionId

#### Get Signature

> **get** **actionId**(): `string`

The id the action was accepted under. Once it dispatches, this equals
`requestId` on the folded message the action derives.

##### Returns

`string`

***

### actorUserId

#### Get Signature

> **get** **actorUserId**(): `string` \| `undefined`

The user who queued it, absent when a bot acted on nobody's behalf.

##### Returns

`string` \| `undefined`

***

### attachments

#### Get Signature

> **get** **attachments**(): `PromptAttachment`[]

Files the prompt refers to; empty for a compact. Kept through an edit.

##### Returns

`PromptAttachment`[]

***

### createdAt

#### Get Signature

> **get** **createdAt**(): `string`

When the action was accepted, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

##### Returns

`string`

***

### kind

#### Get Signature

> **get** **kind**(): `string`

`prompt` or `compact`; only turn-occupying actions are ever queued.

##### Returns

`string`

***

### prompt

#### Get Signature

> **get** **prompt**(): `string` \| `undefined`

The prompt's raw text, present for prompts only. What an edit replaces.

##### Returns

`string` \| `undefined`

symbols.CalendarEvent.addToCalendar:
### addToCalendar()

> **addToCalendar**(`options?`): `Promise`\<`CalendarEvent`\>

Add a snapshot of an event shared with one of the requester's
channels to one of their Google calendars, and return a handle to the
synced snapshot. The snapshot keeps the meeting's iCalendar UID and
organizer, lists only the requester as a guest, and carries no join link;
nobody is notified, and answers or guests on it never reach the meeting.
Refused with `already_on_calendar` when the meeting is already on one of
their calendars, whichever calendar is named, so it cannot be added to
another of their calendars either; with `join_request_open` while their
request to join it is pending or accepted (the meeting then arrives as an
invitation); and with `copy_refused` when Google will not import it.

symbols.CalendarEvent.delete:
### delete()

> **delete**(`options?`): `Promise`\<`void`\>

Delete the event (or a scoped part of a recurring series) at its provider.

A meeting on more than one of the user's inboxes is one event per inbox.
Before deleting any of them, ask the user which inbox's copy to delete,
then pass that copy's `inbox`. Never choose between the user's inboxes
yourself, whatever they look like: a test, secondary or unfamiliar address
is still the user's own inbox. Skip the question only when the user
already named the inbox, or when only one copy can be deleted; then delete
that copy and say why. Without `inbox` the call is refused with
`copy_choice_required`, listing each copy and the question to ask.

Deleting the copy the user organizes cancels the meeting for every guest.
Deleting a copy where they are a guest takes the meeting off that inbox's
calendar: on Google it also declines the invitation and tells the
organizer, while on Outlook the organizer is not told and still sees the
invitation unanswered.

| `options?` | `DeleteEventOptions` |

symbols.CalendarNamespace:
# Class: CalendarNamespace

The calendar surface: the caller's visible calendars, event creation, and
handles to individual events and calendars. Backed by calendar_service (the
SDK reaches it on the gateway's `/calendar` route).

A meeting on more than one of the user's inboxes is one event per inbox;
[CalendarNamespace.occurrences](#occurrences) lists each copy with its `inbox` and
`role`. Before changing such a meeting's details, guests or guest
permissions, or deleting it, ask the user which inbox's copy to change, then
pass that copy's `inbox` to `CalendarEvent.update`,
`CalendarEvent.inviteGuests` or `CalendarEvent.delete`. Never
choose between the user's inboxes yourself, whatever they look like: a
test, secondary or unfamiliar address is still the user's own inbox. Skip
the question only when the user already named the inbox, when only one copy
can make the change, or when adding guests from the copy the user
organizes, and say why. Reminders may go to one copy; name its inbox. Read
those three methods' documentation before changing a meeting held through
several inboxes: it says what each change does from each copy.

`CalendarEvent.addToCalendar` adds a shared meeting only while none
of the user's calendars holds it. Refused with `already_on_calendar`, it is
refused on every calendar, so tell the user the meeting is already on their
calendar and never offer to add it to another one.

the address of the connected inbox holding that copy of the event
(`inbox`) and whether the user organizes it or is a guest there (`role`,
absent when neither). A meeting on several of the user's inboxes appears

never by id.

user's inboxes yourself, whatever they look like. Pass the chosen copy's
`inbox` to its `update`, `inviteGuests` or `delete`; without it the call
is refused with `copy_choice_required`, which names each copy's inbox and
event and gives the question to ask. An occurrence whose calendar is no
longer listed has no `inbox`; take it from that refusal.

each change applies to the whole team. Users without a team have private
labels belonging to their account.

A label's `channelIds` lists only the channels the authenticated user is a
member of. Manual labels count all assignments; smart tags count visible
matches. A channel can be in one manual label and any number of matching
smart tags per team or account. Direct messages cannot be grouped.

symbols.postToChannel:
# Function: postToChannel()

> **postToChannel**(`client`, `target`, `body`): `Promise`\<`string`\>

Post a message using the endpoint supported by the caller's credentials.

Most credentials use `POST /messages/channel/{id}`. User-owned bots without
an acting user instead use `POST /channels/{id}/webhook`, which authorizes
through channel membership. The bot owner is read from `GET /bots/me` and
cached by the client.

The webhook endpoint supports content only. Mentions in `<m-*>` tags still
work, but threads and attachments are not supported.

Posting to a `Thread` puts the message in that thread; to a `Channel`, at the
channel root. One target rather than a channel plus a thread id, so the two
can't disagree.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `client` | `MacroClient` |
| `target` | `Channel` \| `Thread` |
| `body` | `RichMessage` |

## Returns

`Promise`\<`string`\>

symbols.EmailThread.addEventToCalendar:
### addEventToCalendar()

> **addEventToCalendar**(`message`, `invitation`, `options?`): `Promise`\<`CalendarEvent`\>

Add a shared event one of this thread's messages carries (a published
`.ics`, such as one sent with Forward by email) to one of the
requester's Google calendars, and return a handle to the synced
snapshot. The event is read from the saved message, never from the
caller, and lands the way `CalendarEvent.addToCalendar` adds a
channel-shared one: the meeting's iCalendar UID and organizer, only the
requester as a guest, no join link, nobody notified. Refused with
`invalid_input` for an invitation, which is answered from the calendar
instead, `already_on_calendar` when the meeting is already on one of
their calendars, whichever calendar is named (it cannot be added to
another of theirs either), and `copy_refused` when Google will not

symbols.Webhook: # Class: Webhook A webhook registration: an HTTPS endpoint Macro delivers signed entity events to. A free-to-construct `(client, id)` handle like any other entity: the detail record loads lazily from the webhook GET endpoint on first field access and is dropped after any mutation. WebhooksNamespace.list enumerates the caller's webhooks across their personal and team workspaces. The signing secret is only ever returned once, from [create](#create); it's exposed there as [Webhook.signingSecret](#property-signingsecret). Save it — patches, gets, and `byId` handles never carry it again — and pass it to `MacroOpts.webhookSecret` so `macro.events.webhook()` can verify deliveries. Live SSE via `macro.events.listen()` does not use a persisted webhook or signing secret. ## Extends - `MacroEntity`\<`storage.Webhook`\> ## Properties | Property | Modifier | Type | Description | Inherited from | | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ | ------ | | `createdAt` | `readonly` | () => `Promise`\<`string`\> | When the webhook was created. | - | | `createdBy` | `readonly` | () => `Promise`\<`User`\> | The user who registered this webhook. | - | | `endpointUrl` | `readonly` | () => `Promise`\<`string`\> | The HTTPS endpoint URL deliveries are sent to. | - | | `filters` | `readonly` | () => `Promise`\<`storage.Vec`\> | The event/entity-id filters that gate deliveries. | - | | `id` | `public readonly` | `string` | - | `MacroEntity.id` | | `isValid` | `readonly` | () => `Promise`\<`boolean`\> | Whether the current endpoint configuration has passed validation. | - | | `name` | `readonly` | () => `Promise`\<`string`\> | The webhook's display name. | - | | `namespace` | `readonly` | () => `Promise`\<`string`\> | The caller-chosen namespace, unique among the owning workspace's webhooks. Fixed at creation time; it cannot be patched. | - | | `signingSecret?` | `readonly` | `string` | The signing secret used to verify deliveries, present only on the handle returned by [create](#create). `undefined` for `byId` and listed handles. | - | | `status` | `readonly` | () => `Promise`\<`WebhookStatus`\> | The webhook's lifecycle status. | - | | `workspaceId` | `readonly` | () => `Promise`\<`string`\> | The owning workspace id: the creator's user id for a personal webhook, or a team id for a team webhook. | - |

symbols.MacroEvents.listen:
### listen()

> **listen**(`opts?`): `Promise`\<() => `void`\>

Open a live Server-Sent Events stream of matching broker events. This is
the default way to receive events — no public URL or signing secret
required. Delivery is best-effort: events published before the
connection, while disconnected, or dropped for a slow subscriber are
missed; there is no replay.

Filters default to the event names currently registered with [on](#on).
The stream uses those filters for its lifetime; later `.on` / unsubscribe
calls do not change what the server sends.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `opts?` | `ListenOptions` |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<() => `void`\>

symbols.MacroEvents.onSelfMention:
### onSelfMention()

> **onSelfMention**(`handler`): () => `void`

Subscribe to @-mentions of the authenticated caller: `message.mentioned`
deliveries whose mentioned entity is this bot (bot auth) or this user
(user auth), in channels and in document comments alike.

`message.mentioned` deliveries cover every mention the stream's (or
webhook's) workspace can access (its `ids` filter holds channel or
document ids); picking out "me" happens here, client-side. The caller's
identity is resolved lazily (once) on the first delivery.

For SSE, register this handler before [listen](#listen) so the derived
filters include `message.mentioned`. For persisted webhooks, register the
webhook separately, e.g. `macro.webhooks.create({ filters: [{ events:
['message.mentioned'] }], … })`.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `handler` | `EventHandler`\<`"message.mentioned"`\> |

#### Returns

An unsubscribe function.

() => `void`

symbols.msg:
# Function: msg()

> **msg**(`strings`, ...`values`): `RichMessage`

Compose a rich message. Interpolate mentions (a User, Document,
`here`, …) or plain strings. Each mention writes its `<m-*>` tag into the
content *and* adds itself to `mentions[]`, so the two can never drift; strings
are inserted as-is, so markdown like `**bold**` passes through untouched.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type |
| ------ | ------ |
| `strings` | `TemplateStringsArray` |
| ...`values` | `Interpolation`[] |

## Returns

`RichMessage`

## Example

```ts
channel.send(msg`Hey ${user}, see ${doc}. cc ${here}`);
channel.send(msg`Status: ${status} — see ${doc}`);
```
